meta_title: Canadian Passport Photo Size (50×70 mm) & Requirements | Resize-It
meta_description: Canadian passport photos are 50 × 70 mm with a 31–36 mm face, white or light background, under 6 months old, with photographer details on the back. All rules explained.
h1: Canadian Passport Photo Size and Requirements
subtitle: Check your framing at 50 × 70 mm against the IRCC rules before your photographer appointment.

tool_workspace.description: Upload a photo to crop it to the official size. Everything is processed in your browser; nothing is uploaded.

rows.label: Photo size
rows.value: 50 mm wide × 70 mm high (2 in × 2¾ in)

rows.label: Background
rows.value: Plain white or light-coloured, clearly different from your face

rows.label: How recent
rows.value: Taken no more than 6 months before you apply

rows.label: Who takes it
rows.value: A commercial photographer, professionally printed on plain, high-quality photo paper. Home prints are not accepted.

rows.label: Back of photo
rows.value: Photographer stamps or writes the date and studio name and address. Your guarantor certifies one photo (not needed for adult renewals).

rows.label: Glasses
rows.value: Allowed if your eyes are clearly visible with no glare. Tinted lenses and sunglasses are not accepted.

rows.label: Expression
rows.value: Neutral: eyes open, mouth closed, not smiling or frowning

rows.label: Online renewal
rows.value: JPEG from the original camera file, 3:2 portrait, 1,200 × 1,800 to 3,000 × 4,500 px, 200 KB–5 MB, head 45–50% of the height

notes: Canada requires photos taken by a commercial photographer, and any editing (including cropping, background changes or AI tools) is prohibited. Use this page to check your framing and the rules; the photos you submit must come from the photographer.
Headwear is accepted only if worn daily for religious or medical reasons, with your full face visible.
If you use a wheelchair, place a plain white cover over the headrest.
Newborns may be photographed in a car seat with a white blanket behind the head and no shadows.
requirements.checked: Checked against these sources in November 2026. Rules change, so confirm on the official page before you apply.

how_to.title: How to make a Canadian passport photo
how_to.step1_text: Stand in front of a plain background in even light and have someone else take the photo at eye level. Follow the Canadian rules below.
how_to.step2_text: Choose the photo. It is processed in your browser and never uploaded to a server.
how_to.step3_text: Drag the frame to centre your face and use Zoom until your head fills the frame to the size the rules require.
how_to.step4_text: Download the PDF sheet and print it at actual size (100%, no "fit to page") on photo paper, then cut out the photos.

items.q: What size is a Canadian passport photo?
items.a: 50 mm wide by 70 mm high (2 × 2¾ inches), with your face 31–36 mm from chin to crown.

items.q: Can I take my own Canadian passport photo?
items.a: No. Photos must be taken by a commercial photographer and professionally printed. For online renewal, the digital photo must also come from a studio, saved straight from the original camera file.

items.q: What goes on the back of the photo?
items.a: The photographer adds the date and the studio name and address. Your guarantor writes "I certify this to be a true likeness of (your name)" and signs. The guarantor part is not needed for adult renewals.
Yes, if your eyes are clearly visible and there is no glare. Tinted lenses and sunglasses are not accepted.
